proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(P_O\) be the stipulated observable distribution, and let \(\mathsf P_0\in\mathfrak M_H\) be the admitted sustained-arm full-data extension fixed in the statement. Write \(U_0\) for its response table and \(C_0\) for its censoring time. The finite horizon has finitely many treatment branches and time coordinates, and each raw count coordinate lies in the countable set \(\mathbb Z_+\). Thus the response-type space is countable, and the conditional probability kernels used below exist by discrete conditioning.

First retain jointly and without modification the two sustained raw histories in \(U_0\). On \(\{S_k^1=1,B=b,T=t\}\), define a draw \(\widetilde W\) by
\[
 \mathsf P(\widetilde W=w\mid U_0)
 =\frac{\gamma_{btw}}{p_{bt}}\quad\text{if }p_{bt}>0.     \tag{1}
\]
If \(p_{bt}=0\), the event being conditioned on has probability zero and the conditional law can be arbitrary. The row-margin constraint in \(\text{def:triple-polytope}\) states \(\sum_w\gamma_{btw}=p_{bt}\), so (1) is a probability mass function on every positive cell. It follows that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\mathsf P(B=b,T=t,\widetilde W=w\mid S_k^1=1)\\
 &\qquad=p_{bt}\frac{\gamma_{btw}}{p_{bt}}=\gamma_{btw}
 \end{aligned}                                           \tag{2}
\]
when \(p_{bt}>0\), while both sides vanish when \(p_{bt}=0\). Hence the constructed triple margin is \(\gamma\). Summing (2) over \((b,t)\) and using the column-margin constraint in \(\text{def:triple-polytope}\) gives
\[
 \mathsf P(\widetilde W=w\mid S_k^1=1)
 =\sum_{b,t}\gamma_{btw}=q_w.                            \tag{3}
\]

We next implement the cap-fibre part of \(\mathfrak L\). Under the retained standard sustained history put
\[
 Z=Y_K^0-Y_k^0\quad\text{on }\{S_k^0=1\}.               \tag{4}
\]
The landmark-survival positivity condition makes the conditional law in (4) well defined. By the definition of \(q_w\),
\[
 q_w=\mathsf P_0\{\min(Z,H)=w\mid S_k^0=1\}.             \tag{5}
\]
For \(q_w>0\), let \(\kappa_w\) be the conditional law in (5) further conditioned on \(Z\); for \(q_w=0\), use any law supported on the same cap fibre. Conditional on \(\widetilde W=w\), draw \(\widetilde Z\) from \(\kappa_w\). Applying \(\text{lem:cap-fibre-mixture}\) to the conditional standard-survivor law in (5) and the mass identity (3) yields
\[
 \min\{\widetilde Z,H\}=\widetilde W\quad\text{almost surely}, \tag{6}
\]
and, for every \(z\in\mathbb Z_+\),
\[
 \mathsf P(\widetilde Z=z\mid S_k^1=1)
 =\mathsf P_0(Z=z\mid S_k^0=1).                          \tag{7}
\]
Equation (7) is stronger than required for the corrected target: it records the uncapped residual equality used by the sharp-transfer result below.

Construct the switched raw history as follows. Through time \(k\), copy the sustained intensive history exactly, as required by \(\text{ass:no-anticipation}\). If death has occurred by \(k\), continue the absorbing death state and add no later events. If the unit is alive at \(k\), keep this otherwise unobserved branch alive through \(K\), add exactly \(\widetilde Z\) raw events at time \(k+1\), and keep its count constant thereafter. The inequality \(K\ge k+1\) makes this time available; \(\widetilde Z\in\mathbb Z_+\) makes the count nondecreasing; and the raw-path model permits multiple events in one interval. The branch is therefore legal and its raw post-landmark increment is \(\widetilde Z\). By (6), its separately capped residual is
\[
 W=\min\{Y_K^{1\to0}-Y_k^{1\to0},H\}
   =\min\{\widetilde Z,H\}=\widetilde W.                \tag{8}
\]
The support constraint \(\gamma_{btw}=0\) when \(b+w>H\), together with (2) and (8), gives
\[
 \mathsf P(B+W\le H\mid S_k^1=1)=1,                     \tag{9}
\]
which is exactly \(\text{ass:capped-capacity}\). When \(W=H\), the draw \(\widetilde Z\) may exceed \(H\); likewise the retained raw count at \(k\) may exceed \(H\). Thus (8)--(9) impose no global raw-count cap.

It remains to complete a finite response tree. Index a node at time \(\ell\) by its treatment prefix through \(\ell\). Place the retained sustained histories and the switched history just constructed on their prescribed prefix nodes. These prescriptions agree on every shared prefix: the switched and intensive paths agree through \(k\) by construction, and all retained paths came from the valid table \(U_0\). Traverse every remaining prefix node in increasing time order. At each unset child, copy its parent's count and death state; append an alive, zero-event state when the parent is alive and the absorbing state when it is dead. Every node has a unique parent, so the recursion is well defined. Values at time \(\ell\) depend only on the treatment prefix through \(\ell\); hence the resulting table \(U'\) is an FFRCISTG response tree. Each branch has nondecreasing integer counts and absorbing death.

To check randomization and censoring without silently imposing an NPSEM product structure, sample \((U_0,R,C_0)\) under its original law, sample the two auxiliary variables above from kernels depending on \(U_0\) but not on \(R\), and set \(C=C_0\). If \(E\) is any event in the completed response-table space, baseline randomization for \(\mathsf P_0\) gives, for \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathsf P(U'\in E,R=a)
 &=\int \mathsf P(U'\in E\mid U_0=u)\,
       \mathsf P_0(R=a,U_0\in du)\\
 &=\mathsf P_0(R=a)\int \mathsf P(U'\in E\mid U_0=u)\,
       \mathsf P_0(U_0\in du)\\
 &=\mathsf P_0(R=a)\mathsf P(U'\in E).
 \end{aligned}                                           \tag{10}
\]
Thus \(R\perp U'\), as required by \(\text{ass:baseline-randomization}\), and the positive assignment probabilities in \(\text{ass:assignment-positivity}\) are unchanged.

For \(R=a\), the factual sustained branch of \(U'\) is exactly the corresponding branch of \(U_0\), and \(C=C_0\). Consequently
\[
 (R,C,\mathcal H_K^R)\ \text{has the same joint law under }
 \mathsf P\text{ and }\mathsf P_0.                       \tag{11}
\]
By \(\text{ass:consistency}\), truncating that factual path at \(C\) produces \(O\); hence (11) proves equality of the complete observed pushforward, not merely equality of a terminal summary. For every \(a\) and \(\ell\), on the positive-probability factual at-risk event specified in the assumptions, (11) and \(\text{ass:censoring-exchangeability}\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\mathsf P(C\ge\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,D_{\ell-1}^a=0,
                         \mathcal H_K^a)\\
 &=\mathsf P_0(C\ge\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,D_{\ell-1}^a=0,
                           \mathcal H_K^a)\\
 &=\mathsf P_0(C\ge\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,D_{\ell-1}^a=0,
                           \mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a)\\
 &=\mathsf P(C\ge\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,D_{\ell-1}^a=0,
                         \mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a).
 \end{aligned}                                           \tag{12}
\]
The common continuation probability in (12) is strictly positive by \(\text{ass:censoring-positivity}\). The sustained survival probabilities are also unchanged and remain positive by \(\text{ass:landmark-survival-positivity}\). Equations (3), (8), and (9) verify \(\text{ass:capped-residual-transportability}\) and \(\text{ass:capped-capacity}\); the prefix construction verifies \(\text{ass:no-anticipation}\), nondecreasing counts, and absorbing death. Thus every condition in \(\text{def:model-class}\) holds.

No independence between \(C\) and the full response table was used: retaining \(C_0\) preserves whatever dependence on the original unassigned branches was present, subject only to (12). Likewise, the auxiliary conditional kernels construct one witness and are not asserted as cross-world restrictions on the class.

Conversely, let \(\mathsf P\in\mathfrak M_H\). The positivity condition \(\mathsf P(S_k^1=1)>0\) permits the definition
\[
 \gamma_{btw}=\mathsf P(B=b,T=t,W=w\mid S_k^1=1).         \tag{13}
\]
Its \((B,T)\) margin is \(p_{bt}\) by definition. Its \(W\) margin is \(q_w\) by \(\text{ass:capped-residual-transportability}\). Finally, \(\text{ass:capped-capacity}\) makes (13) vanish whenever \(b+w>H\). These are exactly the nonnegativity, margin, and support constraints in \(\text{def:triple-polytope}\), so \(\gamma\in\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\). This proves the converse and completes the corrected target.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(Z\) be \(\mathbb Z_+\)-valued, let \(q_w=\mathsf P(\min\{Z,H\}=w)\) for \(w\in\mathbb I_H\), and let \(W\) have mass function \(q\). For \(q_w>0\), let \(\kappa_w\) be the conditional law of \(Z\) given \(\min\{Z,H\}=w\); for \(q_w=0\), let \(\kappa_w\) be any probability law supported on \(\{z\in\mathbb Z_+:\min\{z,H\}=w\}\). If \(\widetilde Z\) conditional on \(W=w\) has law \(\kappa_w\), then \(\min\{\widetilde Z,H\}=W\) almost surely and \(\widetilde Z\) has the same law as \(Z\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For each \(w\in\mathbb I_H\), the fibre \(F_w=\{z\in\mathbb Z_+:\min\{z,H\}=w\}\) is nonempty: it is \(\{w\}\) when \(w<H\), and it is \(\{H,H+1,\ldots\}\) when \(w=H\). Hence every \(\kappa_w\) in the statement exists and is supported on \(F_w\). Conditional support therefore gives
\[
 \mathsf P\{\min(\widetilde Z,H)=W\mid W=w\}=1
 \quad\text{for every }w\text{ with }q_w>0.               \tag{1}
\]
The remaining values of \(w\) have probability zero, so (1) proves \(\min\{\widetilde Z,H\}=W\) almost surely. For any \(z\in\mathbb Z_+\), the law of total probability and \(\mathsf P(W=w)=q_w\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathsf P(\widetilde Z=z)
 &=\sum_{w=0}^{H}q_w\kappa_w(\{z\})\\
 &=\sum_{w:q_w>0}\mathsf P\{\min(Z,H)=w\}
      \mathsf P\{Z=z\mid\min(Z,H)=w\}\\
 &=\mathsf P(Z=z).
 \end{aligned}                                           \tag{2}
\]
The terms with \(q_w=0\) vanish, so their arbitrary conditional laws do not affect (2). Equality at every atom of the countable support \(\mathbb Z_+\) proves equality of laws.
added_lemmas.justification: This elementary mixture identity is the load-bearing bridge from a capped coupling to the published uncapped residual equality.
added_lemmas.gap: A capped marginal alone does not specify which uncapped values in the top fibre are used; the conditional-fibre kernel supplies an explicit law-preserving choice.
added_lemmas.consumer: The response-tree lift and the raw-no-carry-over sharp-transfer corollary use the identity.

added_lemmas.statement: For every \(\delta\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}\), \(\mathcal R(\delta)=\max_{j\in\mathcal M}h_{\mathcal V}(\delta-e_j)\). Hence \(\Delta^\star\) is nonempty and is exactly the set of \(\delta\)-coordinates solving the explicit epigraph program \(\min_{\delta,\rho}\rho\) subject to \(\delta_m\ge0\), \(\sum_m\delta_m=1\), and \(\rho\ge h_{\mathcal V}(\delta-e_j)\) for every \(j\in\mathcal M\); each constraint is evaluated by the eligibility-greedy support algorithm. In \(\mathsf E_3\), the unique randomized minimax distribution is \((\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3)=(9/16,5/16,1/8)\), with \(\mathcal R(\delta)=17/160<7/40=\min_mR_m\). Moreover, on a relatively open neighborhood of \(\mathsf E_3\) in \(\Theta_3\), randomized minimax regret remains strictly smaller than the regret of every deterministic threshold.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\delta\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}\). For \(e_j\) the \(j\)-th standard basis vector, finiteness of \(\mathcal M\) permits the interchange
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal R(\delta)
 &=\sup_{v\in\mathcal V}\left\{\sum_m\delta_mv_m-min_jv_j\right\}\\
 &=\sup_{v\in\mathcal V}\max_{j\in\mathcal M}(\delta-e_j)^\top v\\
 &=\max_{j\in\mathcal M}\sup_{v\in\mathcal V}(\delta-e_j)^\top v
 =\max_{j\in\mathcal M}h_{\mathcal V}(\delta-e_j).
 \end{aligned}                                           \tag{1}
\]
The third expression and the last expression are both the supremum over \(\mathcal V\times\mathcal M\). By \(\text{thm:joint-value-set-and-support}\), \(\mathcal V\) is compact. Its support function is therefore finite and continuous, since
\[
 |h_{\mathcal V}(\lambda)-h_{\mathcal V}(\lambda')|
 \le \sup_{v\in\mathcal V}\|v\|_2\,\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_2. \tag{2}
\]
Equation (1) is a finite maximum of continuous convex functions of \(\delta\). The simplex \(\Delta_{\mathcal M}\) is nonempty and compact, so a minimizer exists. Introducing the scalar epigraph variable \(\rho\) gives exactly the variables and constraints displayed in the theorem. The support oracle in \(\text{thm:eligibility-greedy-support}\) evaluates every constraint.

We now calculate the cap-three instance exactly. The following three plans have the margins in \(\mathsf E_3\), are nonnegative, and use only cells satisfying \(b+w\le3\); all unlisted entries are zero:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|l|c}
 r&\text{nonzero cells of }x^{(r)}&(J_1,J_2,J_3)\\ \hline
 1&x_{02}=1/5, x_{03}=1/5, x_{10}=1/5, x_{11}=1/10,
      x_{21}=1/5, x_{30}=1/10&(3/10,11/20,21/40)\\
 2&x_{01}=1/5, x_{03}=1/5, x_{11}=1/10, x_{12}=1/5,
      x_{20}=1/5, x_{30}=1/10&(1/2,7/20,21/40)\\
 3&x_{00}=1/5, x_{03}=1/5, x_{11}=1/10, x_{12}=1/5,
      x_{21}=1/5, x_{30}=1/10&(7/10,11/20,21/40).
 \end{array}                                               \tag{3}
\]
The displayed values follow by substituting the plans and \((\mu_0,\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3)=(0,7/20,7/40,0)\) into the value map in \(\text{def:threshold-value-set}\).

For an arbitrary \(\delta=(\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3)\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}\), nature may use the three plan--comparator pairs \((x^{(1)},1)\), \((x^{(2)},2)\), and \((x^{(3)},3)\). Their regrets are respectively
\[
 g_1(\delta)=\frac14\delta_2+\frac9{40}\delta_3,\qquad
 g_2(\delta)=\frac3{20}\delta_1+\frac7{40}\delta_3,\qquad
 g_3(\delta)=\frac7{40}\delta_1+\frac1{40}\delta_2.     \tag{4}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal R(\delta)\ge\max_r g_r(\delta)\). The positive convex combination
\[
 \frac38g_1(\delta)+\frac18g_2(\delta)+\frac12g_3(\delta)
 =\frac{17}{160}(\delta_1+\delta_2+\delta_3)
 =\frac{17}{160}                                         \tag{5}
\]
proves the universal lower bound \(\mathcal R(\delta)\ge17/160\).

Set \(\delta^*=(9/16,5/16,1/8)\). For comparator \(j=1,2,3\), the row coefficients \((c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3)\) for the directions \(\delta^*-e_j\) are
\[
 (0,-7/16,-1/8,0),\qquad
 (0,9/16,-1/8,0),\qquad
 (0,9/16,7/8,0),                                          \tag{6}
\]
respectively. Processing columns from \(3\) down to \(0\) and eligible rows in decreasing order of (6) gives, respectively, the three plans in (3). The eligibility-greedy theorem proves that these plans maximize the three support directions, rather than merely furnishing lower bounds. Substitution into (4) gives
\[
 h_{\mathcal V}(\delta^*-e_1)
 =h_{\mathcal V}(\delta^*-e_2)
 =h_{\mathcal V}(\delta^*-e_3)=\frac{17}{160}.            \tag{7}
\]
Equations (1), (5), and (7) prove minimaxity and the stated value.

If another \(\delta\) attained \(17/160\), then each \(g_r(\delta)\le17/160\). Because every weight in (5) is strictly positive and their weighted average already equals \(17/160\), all three inequalities must be equalities. Solving
\[
 g_1(\delta)=g_2(\delta)=g_3(\delta)=17/160,\qquad
 \delta_1+\delta_2+\delta_3=1                            \tag{8}
\]
gives \((\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3)=(9/16,5/16,1/8)\). Hence the randomized minimizer is unique. The exact deterministic calculation in \(\text{prop:rational-recommendation-reversal}\) gives \(\min_mR_m=R_1=7/40=28/160\), so the improvement is strict.

Finally, write \(\vartheta=(\pi,p,\mu,q)\) for a cap-three margin tuple. Near \(\mathsf E_3\), its three nontrivial Hall slacks are strictly positive because at the center they are \((1/5,3/10,1/5)\) and each is linear in \((p,q)\). For fixed \((\delta,j)\), the eligibility-greedy allocations use finitely many row orderings and finitely many row- or column-exhaustion patterns. Within a pattern they are obtained from \((p,q)\) by finite sums, differences, and minima, and the resulting support value is continuous in \((\vartheta,\delta)\). When coefficient orderings meet, the exchanged rows have equal coefficients, so the adjacent objective values agree. Thus the function
\[
 \Phi(\vartheta,\delta)=\max_jh_{\mathcal V_\vartheta}(\delta-e_j) \tag{9}
\]
is jointly continuous on a neighborhood of \(\mathsf E_3\) times the compact simplex. Uniform continuity then implies continuity of \(\min_\delta\Phi(\vartheta,\delta)\). The same finite-pattern argument, restricted to the three simplex vertices, proves continuity of \(\min_mR_m(\vartheta)\). At \(\mathsf E_3\) their difference is \(28/160-17/160=11/160>0\). A sufficiently small relatively open neighborhood inside \(\Theta_3\) preserves its sign, proving the last assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: Randomization is a genuine decision option on a finite policy menu, and its worst-case regret is computable from the same shared-law support oracle.
added_lemmas.gap: The deterministic correspondence does not determine whether mixing thresholds lowers worst-case regret or how to compute the optimal mixture.
added_lemmas.consumer: A robust trial analysis can report all randomized minimax rules and the strict gain over deterministic thresholds in the rational reversal family.

added_lemmas.statement: For every fixed observable distribution of \(O\) and every sustained-arm full-data extension admitted by \(\mathfrak M_H\), restriction to \(\mathfrak M_H^{\mathrm J}\) leaves the conditional identified set of \((B,T,W)\) exactly \(\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\), and its \((B,W)\) projection exactly \(\Gamma_H(p,q)\). Consequently the endpoints in \(\text{thm:sharp-threshold-endpoints}\), the complete value set and support function in \(\text{thm:joint-value-set-and-support}\), and the deterministic and randomized shared-law regret and minimax correspondences are sharp without change on the published raw no-carry-over subclass intersected with \(B+W\le H\). Both inclusions hold at Hall equalities, and no raw count is bounded by \(H\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix the observable distribution and the stipulated sustained-arm extension. Let \(\Theta_{\gamma}^{\mathrm J}\) denote the set of conditional laws of \((B,T,W)\) among intensive survivors generated by laws in \(\mathfrak M_H^{\mathrm J}\) with that observable distribution and sustained-arm extension.

For the first inclusion, \(\mathfrak M_H^{\mathrm J}\subseteq\mathfrak M_H\) by \(\text{def:janvin-raw-no-carryover-subclass}\). The converse direction of \(\text{thm:causal-response-tree-lift}\) therefore gives
\[
 \Theta_{\gamma}^{\mathrm J}\subseteq\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q). \tag{1}
\]
This step uses landmark-survival positivity for conditioning, capped residual transportability for the \(W\) margin, and capped capacity for the support restriction, exactly as verified in that theorem.

For the reverse inclusion, take any \(\gamma\in\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\). The forward construction in \(\text{thm:causal-response-tree-lift}\) preserves the observable distribution and sustained-arm extension and realizes \(\gamma\). Its cap-fibre calculation applies \(\text{lem:cap-fibre-mixture}\) conditionally on the two survivor populations and gives
\[
 \mathcal L(Y_K^{1\to0}-Y_k^{1\to0}\mid S_k^1=1)
 =\mathcal L(Z\mid S_k^0=1).                              \tag{2}
\]
Equation (2), together with membership in \(\mathfrak M_H\), is precisely membership in \(\mathfrak M_H^{\mathrm J}\). Hence
\[
 \mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\subseteq\Theta_{\gamma}^{\mathrm J}. \tag{3}
\]
Combining (1) and (3) proves equality. By \(\text{lem:triple-projection-and-extension}\), projecting this equality onto \((B,W)\) gives exactly \(\Gamma_H(p,q)\).

Every threshold value is the affine map
\[
 J_m=\pi\left\{\sum_{b<m}\mu_b+
                  \sum_{b\ge m,w}wx_{bw}\right\}.       \tag{4}
\]
Therefore equality of the plan set implies equality of every coordinate range and of the full vector image. The attainment argument in \(\text{thm:sharp-threshold-endpoints}\) makes the displayed endpoints sharp, while \(\text{thm:joint-value-set-and-support}\) identifies the full image, its support function, and deterministic regret from that same plan set. Finally, \(\text{thm:randomized-minimax-regret}\) expresses randomized regret entirely through the same support function, so its regret and minimax correspondence are unchanged as well. None of these arguments invokes strict Hall slack. The cap-fibre at \(w=H\) can contain arbitrarily large raw residuals, so equality of the capped plan sets introduces no global raw-count bound.
added_lemmas.justification: This proves maximality relative to the published raw no-carry-over restriction: adding it does not shrink any capped coupling, endpoint, joint value, or regret set.
added_lemmas.gap: Without the cap-fibre construction, sharpness under the broader capped model would not imply sharpness on the published uncapped residual-equality subclass.
added_lemmas.consumer: The comparison with JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 can be stated as an exact sharp extension rather than only as a capped analogue.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every distribution of \(O\) that is the observed-data pushforward of at least one law in \(\mathfrak M_H\), every such sustained-arm full-data extension, and every \(\gamma\in\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\), the explicit algorithm \(\mathfrak L\) produces a finite-horizon FFRCISTG law on raw nonnegative-integer count paths with triple margin \(\gamma\), the same pushforward distribution of \(O\), absorbing death, baseline randomization, and the same arm-specific sequential censoring continuation probabilities conditional on the factual at-risk histories \(\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a\). On each constructed switched survivor branch, \(\min\{Y_K^{1\to0}-Y_k^{1\to0},H\}=W\); the uncapped switched residual may exceed \(H\), and no global restriction bounds raw counts by \(H\). Conversely, every law in \(\mathfrak M_H\) induces a member of \(\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\). The construction imposes neither censoring independence from the entire response tree nor any other cross-world independence beyond baseline randomization and the listed FFRCISTG conditions.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The corrected cap-fibre construction draws an uncapped residual from the standard-arm fibre. When the cap value is H, that raw residual may exceed H, so the old assertion that the raw increment itself equals W is false. The invariant needed by the model and target value is that its cap equals W; the stronger raw marginal equality is proved separately by prop:janvin-subclass-sharp-transfer.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Given an observed-data law with an admitted sustained-arm full-data extension and \(\gamma\in\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\), \(\mathfrak L\) retains the original joint law of the raw intensive and standard sustained histories. Write \(Z=Y_K^0-Y_k^0\) among standard-arm survivors. For each intensive survivor with realized \((B,T)=(b,t)\) and \(p_{bt}>0\), it first draws \(W=w\) with probability \(\gamma_{btw}/p_{bt}\). Conditional on \(W=w\), it then draws an uncapped switched residual \(\widetilde Z\) from the standard-arm conditional law of \(Z\) given \(S_k^0=1\) and \(\min\{Z,H\}=w\); a zero-probability cap fibre uses any law supported on that fibre. It copies the intensive history through \(k\), keeps the otherwise unobserved switched branch alive through \(K\), adds exactly \(\widetilde Z\) raw events immediately after \(k\), and adds none thereafter. For histories dead by \(k\), it continues the absorbing path. It fills every other unused branch by copying the common prefix to its first treatment divergence and then appending a zero-event legal history. It packages the completed prefix-consistent table as \(U\), using auxiliary draws whose conditional law given the original table does not depend on \(R\), and retains the original \((R,C)\). The sustained factual histories and their joint law with \((R,C)\) are therefore unchanged, so the observed pushforward and the original arm-specific sequential coarsening-at-random and positivity conditions are preserved. Zero-probability \((b,t)\) cells use arbitrary conditional values. The construction neither assumes nor requires independence between censoring and unassigned counterfactual branches.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Adding exactly w raw events cannot preserve an uncapped standard residual law with mass above H. Sampling within the observed standard-arm cap fibre preserves both the capped triple and the complete uncapped residual marginal while leaving sustained histories and the observed pushforward fixed.

proposed.name: Published raw no-carry-over capacity subclass
proposed.construction: \(\mathfrak M_H^{\mathrm J}=\{\mathsf P\in\mathfrak M_H:\mathcal L_{\mathsf P}(Y_K^{1\to0}-Y_k^{1\to0}\mid S_k^1=1)=\mathcal L_{\mathsf P}(Z\mid S_k^0=1)\}\), where the equality is equality of probability laws on \(\mathbb Z_+\). Thus the subclass imposes the published uncapped residual no-carry-over equality in addition to, and not in place of, every restriction defining \(\mathfrak M_H\); in particular it retains \(B+W\le H\) almost surely among intensive survivors.

proposed.name: Randomized shared-law regret and minimax correspondence
proposed.construction: Let \(\Delta_{\mathcal M}=\{\delta\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal M|}:\sum_{m\in\mathcal M}\delta_m=1\}\). A draw \(m\sim\delta\), made independently of the latent law, incurs loss \(\sum_m\delta_m v_m\) at \(v\in\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\). Define its shared-law worst-case regret and the randomized minimax correspondence by \(\mathcal R(\delta)=\sup_{v\in\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)}\{\sum_m\delta_m v_m-\min_{j\in\mathcal M}v_j\}\) and \(\Delta^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\delta\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}}\mathcal R(\delta)\).

proposed.name: Observed-law-preserving cap-fibre response-tree gluing handle
proposed.construction: Given an observed-data law with an admitted sustained-arm full-data extension and \(\gamma\in\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\), \(\mathfrak L\) retains the original joint law of the raw intensive and standard sustained histories. Write \(Z=Y_K^0-Y_k^0\) among standard-arm survivors. For each intensive survivor with realized \((B,T)=(b,t)\) and \(p_{bt}>0\), it first draws \(W=w\) with probability \(\gamma_{btw}/p_{bt}\). Conditional on \(W=w\), it then draws an uncapped switched residual \(\widetilde Z\) from the standard-arm conditional law of \(Z\) given \(S_k^0=1\) and \(\min\{Z,H\}=w\); a zero-probability cap fibre uses any law supported on that fibre. It copies the intensive history through \(k\), keeps the otherwise unobserved switched branch alive through \(K\), adds exactly \(\widetilde Z\) raw events immediately after \(k\), and adds none thereafter. For histories dead by \(k\), it continues the absorbing path. It fills every other unused branch by copying the common prefix to its first treatment divergence and then appending a zero-event legal history. It packages the completed prefix-consistent table as \(U\), using auxiliary draws whose conditional law given the original table does not depend on \(R\), and retains the original \((R,C)\). The sustained factual histories and their joint law with \((R,C)\) are therefore unchanged, so the observed pushforward and the original arm-specific sequential coarsening-at-random and positivity conditions are preserved. Zero-probability \((b,t)\) cells use arbitrary conditional values. The construction neither assumes nor requires independence between censoring and unassigned counterfactual branches.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The cap-fibre algorithm changes the construction and adds the uncapped residual symbol Z to its metadata.

proposed.statement: For every distribution of \(O\) that is the observed-data pushforward of at least one law in \(\mathfrak M_H\), every such sustained-arm full-data extension, and every \(\gamma\in\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\), the explicit algorithm \(\mathfrak L\) produces a finite-horizon FFRCISTG law on raw nonnegative-integer count paths with triple margin \(\gamma\), the same pushforward distribution of \(O\), absorbing death, baseline randomization, and the same arm-specific sequential censoring continuation probabilities conditional on the factual at-risk histories \(\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a\). On each constructed switched survivor branch, \(\min\{Y_K^{1\to0}-Y_k^{1\to0},H\}=W\); the uncapped switched residual may exceed \(H\), and no global restriction bounds raw counts by \(H\). Conversely, every law in \(\mathfrak M_H\) induces a member of \(\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\). The construction imposes neither censoring independence from the entire response tree nor any other cross-world independence beyond baseline randomization and the listed FFRCISTG conditions.
proposed.justification: Polyhedral sharpness is causal only if every extremal summary coupling can be realized by a global finite-horizon response tree without silently invoking an NPSEM cross-world product structure.

prose_updates.tldr: A randomized recurrent-event trial identifies separately capped baseline and residual margins while leaving their dependence unknown, and the raw recurrent paths remain unbounded. The externally prespecified sensitivity restriction \(B+W\le H\) creates a Ferrers transport problem and is not implied by separate capping. Dahl2008, Theorem 4, supplies only the reindexed staircase feasibility support. The cap-fibre response-tree construction proves that every feasible triple coupling preserves the observed law and is attainable even after imposing the published uncapped residual no-carry-over equality. The resulting sharp endpoints and common-law value polytope yield exact deterministic and randomized minimax regret; in the cap-three witness the unique randomized rule \((9/16,5/16,1/8)\) has regret \(17/160\), strictly below the best deterministic regret \(7/40\), while scalar intervals select a different deterministic threshold. Confidence-polytope inversion covers the whole value set and all robust optimizers at Hall and policy ties. Uniformly shrinking censoring-adjusted inference is impossible under the frozen pointwise-overlap assumptions; a constructive efficient procedure under quantitative overlap and nuisance-rate conditions remains open.

project_justification.gap: The closest recurrent-event switching analysis supplies a published uncapped no-carry-over equality, threshold-wise scalar sharp bounds, and deterministic decision criteria. Dahl2008, Theorem 4, separately settles staircase fixed-margin feasibility. Neither line proves that every capped coupling has an observed-law-preserving cap-fibre lift within the published raw-no-carry-over subclass, identifies the common latent value law across a threshold menu, or computes the strict deterministic and randomized minimax-regret gains and their boundary-robust confidence sets.
project_justification.fill: The formal kernel combines the attributed Dahl2008 feasibility certificate with an explicit raw-path cap-fibre lift, proves sharp transfer to the published uncapped no-carry-over subclass intersected with the capacity restriction, derives atom-correct endpoints and the common-coupling value polytope, computes deterministic and randomized regret with the eligibility-greedy support oracle, supplies the exact cap-three reversal and unique optimal mixture, and gives simultaneous confidence-set inversion together with a negative uniform-inference limit under pointwise overlap alone.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite vectors \((r_{bt},q_w)\) are identified under factual-arm sequential coarsening at random and may be estimated with censoring adjustment. Under the frozen pointwise-positivity class, uniformly shrinking inference is impossible. A constructive cross-fitted procedure remains open only after adding quantitative effective assignment, survival, and censoring overlap together with explicit nuisance-rate and second-order remainder conditions.

More directly, Dahl2008, Theorem 4 and Section 3, already characterize fixed-margin staircase feasibility and constructions; after reversing the row order, the antidiagonal Hall criterion is exactly that specialization and is not claimed as new. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026 shows the decision relevance of joint payoff geometry and randomization; the present geometry is the image of one capped transport law. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, AndrewsSoares2010, and Gafarov2025 inform confidence inversion at binding inequalities and changing faces. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 supports factual-arm sequential coarsening identification; the proved vanishing-information construction shows that its pointwise assumptions alone cannot furnish nonvacuous uniform inference here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The primitive counts are raw, nonnegative-integer-valued, and not globally bounded by \(H\). The condition \(B+W\le H\) constrains the separately capped prefix burden and switched residual and remains a substantive sensitivity restriction. The cap-fibre lift may draw an uncapped switched residual above \(H\) when \(W=H\); this is essential for preserving the published uncapped standard residual law and is why the theorem asserts equality only after capping. A finite-reserve mechanism gives a compatible class, but no such mechanism or clinically defensible cap has been established for SPRINT. Dahl's feasibility criterion can reject a proposed cap statistically but cannot establish clinical credibility. The response-tree theorem preserves the original arm-specific sequential censoring law on factual at-risk histories and does not assume independence between censoring and the entire cross-world response tree. Finally, pointwise censoring positivity permits vanishing-information sequences, so the negative uniform-inference theorem rules out uniformly shrinking confidence regions under the frozen class; constructive efficient inference requires additional quantitative overlap and nuisance-remainder conditions.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved scope consists of atom-correct endpoints, a raw-path cap-fibre causal lift preserving factual-arm sequential censoring, exact sharp transfer to the published uncapped residual no-carry-over subclass intersected with \(B+W\le H\), the complete common-law value and support characterization, deterministic and randomized minimax regret, the rational recommendation reversal and unique optimal mixture, and confidence-polytope inversion. Dahl2008, Theorem 4, is used only as attributed feasibility support. Uniform inference is resolved negatively under the frozen assumptions by a vanishing-information witness; a nonvacuous cross-fitted or efficient construction under explicit quantitative assignment, survival, censoring-overlap, and nuisance-rate conditions remains open. SPRINT is only a conditional capped-loss consumer: a mechanism and cap must be justified externally and prespecified at \(k=300\), and the application is rejected if no credible capacity interpretation exists or the censoring-adjusted Hall confidence system is infeasible.
